summary: Full extraction of 11 Philippine documents: PRA annual reports 2012, 2017, 2021 and 2025, COA annual audit reports on PRA for 2020-2023 and 2025, the Expanded SRRV leaflet (2025) and the SIRV consular page. Adds the full 1987-2017 yearly and 2017 monthly enrolment/cancellation tables, nationality, age, sex and region splits, visa-deposit series and balances (DBP and private banks), PRA fee income, costs, marketing spend, marketer counts, and SRRV/SIRV fee and deposit rules.

events.title: Export and Industry Bank, a former SRRV depository bank, closed holding retirees' deposits
events.description: COA noted that the de-accredited servicing bank Export and Industry Bank closed in 2012 while holding visa deposits of P33.939 million for 28 retiree-members; PRA had not disclosed it.
events.quote: no accrual for the de-accredited servicing Bank Export and Industry Bank due to its closure in CY 2012

events.title: COA: PRA keeps 87.65% of interest earned on retirees' visa deposits
events.description: COA found that PRA kept 87.65% of the interest earned on retirees' visa deposits at DBP as its own income and credited only 12.35% to the retirees, without basis in the IRR of EO 1037, overstating PRA interest income by P35.293 million in 2022; COA issued an adverse opinion on PRA's 2022 statements.
events.quote: the remaining portion of 87.65 percent became the PRA Share that was recorded as its interest income for the year.

events.title: PRA and Bureau of Immigration sign data sharing agreement
events.description: A Data Sharing Agreement between PRA and the Bureau of Immigration was executed in 2022 for exchange of data and monitoring of resident retirees; no MOA on the visa application process exists (COA 2023).
events.quote: Additionally, in CY 2022, a Data Sharing Agreement was executed between the two agencies

events.title: Retirees' share of interest on visa deposits raised from 2.5% to 5%
events.description: In response to COA findings, PRA raised retirees' share of the interest earned on their DBP visa deposits from 2.5% to 5% in 2024 by internal memorandum; COA found PRA booked P710.123 million of such interest as its own income in 2022-2025 without legal basis.
events.quote: Management increased the retirees’ share of the interest in CY 2024 from 2.5 percent to 5 percent

events.description: PRA introduced a Retirement and Investment Program letting SRRV holders convert visa deposits into business investments within partner economic zones, formalised with the Authority of the Freeport Area of Bataan on 26 March 2025 and the Subic-Clark Alliance for Development on 16 October 2025.

events.title: PRA plans national-security review of the SRRV focusing on Chinese and South Korean nationals

ledger.contains: COA annual audit report on PRA for 2020 and 2019 (125 pp.): executive summary (officers, manpower, financial highlights, budget vs actual, audit opinion bases), auditor report, statement of management responsibility (image), statements of financial position, notes (accounting policies, fee descriptions and processing-fee schedule, investments, receivables, restricted visa-deposit funds, trust liabilities, income by fee, direct costs with marketer numbers, expenses, taxes, leases), Part II observations (trust-liability and restricted-fund reconciliation, leases, fee recognition, visitorial fees, cash in bank, taxes, receivables impairment, de-accredited servicing banks with Table 18, disallowances, disbursement delays, GAD, tax compliance, insurance), Part III status of prior recommendations, Annex A disallowances. Taken: income, fee income by type, interest income, costs (PS, MOOE, direct cost lines), net income, budget vs actual, staff, marketers (and 944/3,276 enrolments already in the data), depository banks, visa deposits (restricted funds by sub-account, trust liabilities PHP/US$), Table 18 deposits and retiree counts at each de-accredited bank, management fees from de-accredited banks, fee rules.
